title: Unify transport adapters across SDKs and prune deprecated API shims
creator: Asha Iyer
description: Background: Over time each language SDK added its own transport layer shims (legacy callbacks, multiple HTTP clients, and in-process retry wrappers). This has increased maintenance cost and produced inconsistent retry/timeout semantics across languages. Goals: 1) Standardize on a small set of supported HTTP transports per language (Python: httpx/urllib fallback; JS: undici/node-fetch polyfill; Go: net/http with configurable client wrappers). 2) Remove deprecated public API shims (legacy sync callbacks, `transportOptions` v1) while preserving compatibility helpers for one release cycle. 3) Pin and bump critical third-party deps to patched versions to address known CVEs and performance regressions.
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs (python/js/go) expose a consistent `Transport`/`Client` abstraction documented in README
Deprecated API shims are removed from public surface; deprecation warnings were emitted in previous release
Automated test matrix (unit + integration) passes for node: 14/16/18, python: 3.9/3.10/3.11, go: 1.20/1.21
Benchmark before/after shows no >10% regression in median latency for small and medium requests
Migration guide added to docs and a short snippet included in SDK CHANGELOGs
technical_notes: Python: replace internal use of `requests` with `httpx` AsyncClient for async paths; keep a thin compatibility layer to handle sync code paths for one more release. Pin httpx to 0.24.x to avoid a known regression in connection pooling discovered in upstream 0.25.0-alpha.

JavaScript: vendor a tiny undici wrapper and remove legacy `node-transport` shim. Expose unified `client.fetch` method across browser and Node via isomorphic adapter. Bump `node-fetch` -> drop-in polyfill only for older Node runtimes.

Go: centralize client creation in internal package runtime/httpclient, expose WithTimeout/WithRetry options. Bump `golang.org/x/net` and `github.com/hashicorp/go-retryablehttp` to patched versions flagged in security audit.
Compatibility: Add a CLI `redwood-sdk-migrate` dev helper that scans repo for deprecated usage patterns and prints suggested replacements (pattern-based heuristics).
Tradeoffs: Keeping thin sync compatibility for Python increases maintenance for one cycle but minimizes customer disruption. Full removal planned next release after migration metrics.
CI changes: add a matrix job that runs smoke tests using the new transports behind a feature flag `USE_MODERN_TRANSPORT` for staged rollout.

Performance testing: run the existing load tester with 1k concurrent connections for python async path vs previous `requests`-based path to validate throughput improvements from httpx connection pooling.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge changes behind feature flag and run full CI matrix (2 days). 2) Deploy SDK release candidate to canary channel and notify top 20 integrators; gather telemetry for 3 days. 3) If no regressions, flip default flag on for new installs and release deprecation-major that removes v1 shims. 4) One-week window where both old and new transports are supported via `compat` package, then remove compat in next major release.
qa_notes: QA should run SDK integration suite against local runtime and hosted API, focusing on: connection resets, idle connection reuse, backoff behavior on 429/503, and header propagation (trace IDs).
Add flaky test guardrails for known intermittent failures; mark platform-dependent tests and run them on dedicated runners.
Verify telemetry tags include `transport=modern` or `transport=legacy` to filter canary vs baseline traffic.
